newsitem.title: USA: CBOT new crop corn ends down on acres, old crop up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT new crop corn ends down on acres, old crop up.

text.p: CBOT new crop corn futures ended sharply lower on higher-than-anticipated USDA corn acreage estimates but old crop months held firm on ideas stocks were tight, traders said.
"A lot of people are saying fact or fiction. Fact are the stocks and fiction is the acreage," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.

USDA on Monday pegged 1997 corn plantings at 81.4 million acres, above trade estimates for 80.9 million. Quarterly stocks were put at 4.494 billion bushels, below analysts' estimates for 4.565 billion.

Floor sources said the quarterly stocks figure suggested feed usage remained strong. They said ending stocks would likely remain below one billion bushels, and added that any number below one billion bushels indicated stocks were tight.

But bulls noted planted acreage was not yet set. Most farmers have not begun planting and wet weather has delayed pesticide application in some areas. "Farmers can change acreage and they will do so depending on weather," said Terry Francl, economist with the American Farm Bureau Federation.
Corn ended five cents per bushel lower to 1-3/4 cents higher with May up 1-3/4 at $3.10 a bushel.
On the day, Dean Witter bought 15 million bushels July and Cargill Inc bought five million December and 2.5 million May, traders said. R.J. O'Brien bought five million July.
Refco Inc sold three million May, seven million July and three million December while Lind-Waldock sold six million December, traders said.
In spread action, Smith Barney spread five million bushels July/December at 16 cents, premium July.

In options trade, FIMAT Futures bought 500 May $2.80 puts at 1/2 cent, Griffin Trading bought 600 December $3.00 calls and sold 600 December $2.50 puts and 600 December $2.60 puts at six cents, floor sources said.
Continental Grain sold 500 December $3.00 calls at 18-1/2 to 19 cents, sources said.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 66,000 contracts, above Thursday's actual volume of 59,910 contracts.
